input.summary: When a user's window expired, `allow` reset the window start but kept the old count. A user who had hit the limit stayed blocked, and their first request in the next window was rejected. I now reset the count to 0 on rollover. A new regression test failed before the fix and passes after it.
input.root_cause: In app/ratelimit.py `allow`, the rollover branch set `start = now` but did not reset `count`, so the stale count carried into the new window.

claims.statement: The code kept the old count on window rollover.
The regression test failed before the fix, at the first request after the window expired.
The fix resets count to 0 when the window rolls over.
After the fix, both tests pass. These are the regression test and the existing test that blocks at the limit within a window.

input.uncertainty: The tests only cover a single user and a single rollover. Boundary behaviour is untested beyond the exact `now - start == window_s` case in the new test.
